verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents standards-based OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 support. It provides a well-known discovery endpoint plus token endpoints that handle refresh tokens through introspection and revocation, and the repo lists a Node.js adapter. Developers therefore rely on a standard provider instead of hand-rolling the protocol, but the specific flows named in the story are not explicitly documented. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the authorization code flow with PKCE, documentation of refresh-token grant/rotation behavior, broader first-party client-library guidance beyond a single Node.js adapter mention, independent hands-on corroboration of these flows.

support.subject: As a developer, I can implement standard OAuth 2.0 / OIDC flows (authorization code with PKCE, refresh tokens) without hand-rolling protocol details

citations.quote: Keycloak is based on standard protocols and provides support for OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, and SAML.
It lists endpoints and other configuration options relevant to the OpenID Connect implementation in Keycloak.
Both refresh tokens and access tokens are supported by this endpoint.
you can use it to validate an access or refresh token
Keycloak Node.js Connect - Node.js adapter for Keycloak
